note: Filed under the noun's consonants because its verbal derivation is uncertain.
summary: בֹּהוּ describes the emptiness of the earth in Genesis 1:2 and of land laid waste in Jeremiah 4:23 and Isaiah 34:11. All three passages pair it with תֹּהוּ.

senses.definition: The emptiness of a place that lies uninhabited or has been laid waste.

evidence.note: תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ describes the earth before the appearance of dry land, vegetation, or animals.
The prophet sees the land as תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ. He looks again and finds no human, the birds gone, and the cities in ruins.
A measuring line of תֹּהוּ and plummet stones of בֹּהוּ are stretched over ruined Edom.

parallels.note: The two nouns qualify corresponding measuring implements in the description of Edom.
